edits.text: - When a marker A immediately precedes a dependent clause (subordinating clause, relative clause, or clausal 'that' complement) that completes, restricts, or names the preceding phrase, and a marker B also exists immediately after that clause, prefer B (the later cut after the clause) over A. This ordering preserves the head plus its clausal complement on the source surface.

Keep dependent clauses attached to their head: when a marker immediately precedes a subordinating, relative, or clausal complement that completes or restricts the preceding phrase, rank the cut after that clause higher than the cut before it (i.e. prefer the later cut).

edits._was: - Is the material after the marker a self-contained constituent (completes a verb, supplies a prepositional complement, names an entity) so that translating separately preserves the whole meaning? If yes, cohesion is likely high; if not, expect damage.
